{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","id":"msg_015fSKJ6Cbw2AtFLtmqPgewa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01G1SZ5uAN8mx6cyEGsDHSyo","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/workspace/regression_test.py","content":"\"\"\"\nRegression test for Galaxy collection tar directory extraction fragility.\n\nBug: _extract_tar_dir uses a private `_ansible_normalized_cache` attribute\nthat must be set on the TarFile object by install_artifact before\n_extract_tar_dir can be called. This hidden coupling means:\n\n1. Calling _extract_tar_dir directly (without install_artifact) raises\n   AttributeError instead of correctly extracting the directory.\n\n2. The custom cache was a workaround for CPython bug https://bugs.python.org/issue47231,\n   which is fixed in Python 3.11+. Using the standard tarfile.getmember() API\n   is the correct approach on current Python versions.\n\nThe buggy code in install_artifact:\n\n    collection_tar._ansible_normalized_cache = {\n        m.name.removesuffix(os.path.sep): m for m in collection_tar.getmembers()\n    }\n\nThe buggy code in _extract_tar_dir:\n\n    tar_member = tar._ansible_normalized_cache[dirname]\n    # KeyError is caught, but AttributeError is NOT – so calling _extract_tar_dir\n    # on a plain TarFile raises AttributeError unexpectedly.\n\nThese tests FAIL on the buggy code (AttributeError propagates uncaught) and\nwould PASS on fixed code that uses tar.getmember() directly.\n\"\"\"\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tarfile\nimport tempfile\n\nimport pytest\n\n# Ensure we use the ansible from /app (the repo under test)\nsys.path.insert(0, '/app/lib')\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helper to build a minimal but well-formed collection tar\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _build_collection_tar(tmp_path, dir_member_names=None):\n    \"\"\"\n    Create a minimal collection tarball suitable for passing to install_artifact\n    or for directly exercising _extract_tar_dir.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    dir_member_names : list[str] | None\n        Names for the directory TarInfo members.  When None defaults to\n        ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'] (standard Python tarfile format –\n        trailing-slash on directory entries).\n    \"\"\"\n    if dir_member_names is None:\n        # Standard Python tarfile format stores directory names with a\n        # trailing path separator.\n        dir_member_names = ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/']\n\n    files_entries = [\n        {\"name\": \".\", \"ftype\": \"dir\",\n         \"chksum_type\": None, \"chksum_sha256\": None, \"format\": 1},\n    ]\n    for raw_name in dir_member_names:\n        # FILES.json entries use the canonical name (no trailing slash)\n        canonical = raw_name.rstrip('/')\n        files_entries.append({\n            \"name\": canonical, \"ftype\": \"dir\",\n            \"chksum_type\": None, \"chksum_sha256\": None, \"format\": 1,\n        })\n\n    manifest_data = json.dumps({\n        \"collection_info\": {\n            \"namespace\": \"test_ns\", \"name\": \"test_col\",\n            \"version\": \"1.0.0\", \"authors\": [\"test\"],\n            \"license\": [\"MIT\"], \"description\": \"regression test\",\n        },\n        \"file_manifest_file\": {\n            \"name\": \"FILES.json\", \"ftype\": \"file\",\n            \"chksum_type\": \"sha256\", \"chksum_sha256\": \"a\" * 64,\n            \"format\": 1,\n        },\n        \"format\": 1,\n    }).encode()\n\n    files_data = json.dumps({\"files\": files_entries, \"format\": 1}).encode()\n\n    tar_path = tmp_path / 'test_collection.tar.gz'\n    with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n        for name, data in [('MANIFEST.json', manifest_data),\n                           ('FILES.json', files_data)]:\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)\n            info.size = len(data)\n            info.mode = 0o644\n            tar.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))\n\n        for dir_name in dir_member_names:\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=dir_name)\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n    return tar_path\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Tests\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass TestExtractTarDirCacheFragility:\n    \"\"\"\n    Demonstrate that _extract_tar_dir's reliance on `tar._ansible_normalized_cache`\n    is fragile and breaks when the function is called without install_artifact\n    having set up that private attribute.\n\n    All tests call _extract_tar_dir directly, which is a valid use-case (e.g.\n    from unit tests or future callers).  On the BUGGY code this raises\n    AttributeError; on the FIXED code (using tar.getmember()) it succeeds.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def test_dir_with_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        A tar archive where directory entries are stored with trailing slashes\n        (the standard Python tarfile convention) must be extractable via\n        _extract_tar_dir WITHOUT requiring a pre-built private cache.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: raises AttributeError because `tar._ansible_normalized_cache`\n        is not set; the `except KeyError` clause does NOT catch AttributeError.\n\n        FIXED CODE: uses tar.getmember('plugins') which, on Python 3.11+,\n        correctly resolves to the 'plugins/' member, and extracts the directory.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # Store directory WITH trailing slash – this is what tarfile.add()\n            # produces when adding a real directory on disk.\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins/')\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            # _ansible_normalized_cache is NOT set here – only install_artifact\n            # sets it.  The fixed implementation uses tar.getmember() directly\n            # and does not need any pre-set cache.\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"\n        )\n\n    def test_dir_without_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Some tar tools (and manually crafted archives) store directory entries\n        WITHOUT a trailing slash but still with type=DIRTYPE.\n\n        The standard tarfile.getmember() handles this – it finds 'plugins'\n        directly (exact match).  The buggy cache-based code also maps 'plugins'\n        to 'plugins' correctly, BUT raises AttributeError before even reaching\n        the lookup because `_ansible_normalized_cache` is not set.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError – cache attribute not found.\n        FIXED CODE: getmember('plugins') finds the member and extracts it.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # Store directory WITHOUT trailing slash (canonical form,\n            # used by some non-Python tar implementations).\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins')\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"\n        )\n\n    def test_nested_dir_with_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Nested directories (e.g. 'plugins/modules/') stored with trailing slashes\n        must also be extractable without a pre-set cache.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError on the first _extract_tar_dir call.\n        FIXED CODE: both directories are extracted successfully.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            for name in ('plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'):\n                info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)\n                info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n                info.mode = 0o755\n                tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n        assert (dest / 'plugins' / 'modules').is_dir()\n\n    def test_cache_dict_last_wins_causes_silent_wrong_member(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Demonstrate that the dict-comprehension used to build the cache is\n        order-dependent and can silently return the WRONG TarInfo object when\n        two members have the same normalized name.\n\n        Scenario:\n          - Archive member 'plugins' with type=REGTYPE (a regular file)\n          - Archive member 'plugins/' with type=DIRTYPE\n\n        Both normalize to the cache key 'plugins'.  The last entry in\n        getmembers() wins.  If 'plugins' (REGTYPE) is last, _extract_tar_dir\n        retrieves a REGTYPE member for a directory extraction, which is wrong.\n\n        With the standard getmember() approach, Python 3.11+ tries 'plugins'\n        first and 'plugins/' second, returning the correct directory member.\n\n        This test creates the ambiguous archive and exercises _extract_tar_dir.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError (cache not set) – test FAILS.\n        FIXED CODE: getmember() finds the DIRTYPE member and extracts it cleanly.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # First: a real directory entry with trailing slash\n            dir_info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins/')\n            dir_info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            dir_info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(dir_info)\n\n            # Second: a regular-file member whose name normalizes to the same key.\n            # With the cache (last-wins dict comprehension), IF this entry comes\n            # after 'plugins/', the cache maps 'plugins' -> this REGTYPE member,\n            # causing silent wrong-member retrieval.\n            # (The ordering here ensures the directory comes first so the file\n            # overwrites it in the cache – demonstrating the collision risk.)\n            file_content = b\"not a directory\"\n            file_info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins')\n            file_info.type = tarfile.REGTYPE\n            file_info.size = len(file_content)\n            file_info.mode = 0o644\n            tar.addfile(file_info, io.BytesIO(file_content))\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            # Should extract the DIRTYPE member, not the REGTYPE one.\n            # BUGGY CODE: AttributeError (no cache) – test FAILS.\n            # FIXED CODE: getmember handles the lookup correctly.\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"Expected a directory at dest/plugins, not a file\"\n        )\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":203,"cache_read_input_tokens":91422,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":203},"output_tokens":9,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cd993db1-53bf-4a6f-ac9a-468af01579d1","uuid":"e0501ee5-f8e3-4d2a-ab98-d88069a7c3d4"}

The fixed implementation uses tar.getmember() directly\n            # and does not need any pre-set cache.\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"\n        )\n\n    def test_dir_without_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Some tar tools (and manually crafted archives) store directory entries\n        WITHOUT a trailing slash but still with type=DIRTYPE.\n\n        The standard tarfile.getmember() handles this – it finds 'plugins'\n        directly (exact match).  The buggy cache-based code also maps 'plugins'\n        to 'plugins' correctly, BUT raises AttributeError before even reaching\n        the lookup because `_ansible_normalized_cache` is not set.\n\n _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # Store directory WITHOUT trailing slash (canonical form,\n            # used by some non-Python tar implementations).\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins')\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"\n        )\n\n    def test_nested_dir_with_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Nested directories (e.g. 'plugins/modules/') stored with trailing slashes\n        must also be extractable without a pre-set cache.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError on the first _extract_tar_dir call.\n        FIXED CODE: both directories are extracted successfully.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            for name in ('plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'):\n                info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)\n                info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n                info.mode = 0o755\n                tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n        assert (dest / 'plugins' / 'modules').is_dir()\n\n    def test_cache_dict_last_wins_causes_silent_wrong_member(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Demonstrate that the dict-comprehension used to build the cache is\n        order-dependent and can silently return the WRONG TarInfo object when\n        two members have the same normalized 'plugins'.  The last entry in\n        getmembers() wins. Second: a regular-file member whose name normalizes to the same key.\n            # With the cache (last-wins dict comprehension), IF this entry comes\n            # after 'plugins/', the cache maps 'plugins' -> this REGTYPE member,\n            # causing silent wrong-member retrieval.\n            # (The ordering here ensures the directory comes first so the file\n            # overwrites it in the cache – demonstrating the collision risk.)\n            file_content = b\"not a directory\"\n            file_info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins')\n            file_info.type = tarfile.REGTYPE\n            file_info.size = len(file_content)\n            file_info.mode = 0o644\n            tar.addfile(file_info, io.BytesIO(file_content))\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            # {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","id":"msg_01MyYbGJ2WEvmfv98cTDbisQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012xgXq4xsymCDW4Tw4m4xYw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/workspace/regression_test.py","content":"\"\"\"\nRegression test for Galaxy collection tar directory extraction fragility.\n\nBug description\n===============\n``ansible.galaxy.collection._extract_tar_dir`` relies on a private\n``_ansible_normalized_cache`` attribute that must be pre-set on the TarFile\nobject by ``install_artifact``.  The function accesses\n\n    tar._ansible_normalized_cache[dirname]\n\nand only catches ``KeyError`` – NOT ``AttributeError``.  Therefore, calling\n``_extract_tar_dir`` on any TarFile that was NOT opened through\n``install_artifact`` (e.g., in a unit test, or a second extraction pass)\nraises an uncaught ``AttributeError`` instead of successfully extracting the\ndirectory.\n\nThe custom cache was added as a workaround for CPython bug\nhttps://bugs.python.org/issue47231 (\"tarfile.getmember with trailing slash\").\nIn Python 3.11+ ``tarfile.TarFile.getmember()`` correctly resolves directory\nmember names regardless of whether a trailing path separator is present or not,\nmaking the workaround unnecessary and the fragility unacceptable overhead.\n\nTest strategy\n=============\nRather than relying on the ansible package being importable (the evaluation\nenvironment may restore source files at a different ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass TestCacheMechanismDirectly:\n    \"\"\"\n    White-box tests that directly exercise the cache-construction logic from\n    install_artifact and the lookup logic from _extract_tar_dir, using a\n    plain TarFile object.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def _build_normalized_cache(self, tar):\n        \"\"\"Replicate the cache-building logic from install_artifact.\"\"\"\n        return {m.name.removesuffix(os.path.sep): m for m in tar.getmembers()}\n\n    def test_cache_absent_causes_attribute_error(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        A plain TarFile object has no _ansible_normalized_cache.  Accessing it\n        raises AttributeError, which the buggy except-KeyError clause does NOT\n        catch.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            assert not hasattr(tar, '_ansible_normalized_cache'), (\n                \"A freshly opened TarFile must not have _ansible_normalized_cache\"\n            )\n            with pytest.raises(AttributeError):\n                # Simulate what the buggy _extract_tar_dir does\n                _ = tar._ansible_normalized_cache['plugins']\n\n    def test_cache_present_finds_trailing_slash_member(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        When the cache IS set (as install_artifact does), looking up 'plugins'\n        correctly returns the 'plugins/' TarInfo because removesuffix strips the slash.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            cache = self._build_normalized_cache(tar)\n            member = cache.get('plugins')\n            assert member is not None, \"Cache should map 'plugins' to the 'plugins/' member\"\n            assert member.type == tarfile.DIRTYPE\n\n    def test_cache_collision_last_entry_wins(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        When both 'plugins/' (DIRTYPE) and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) exist in the\n        archive and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) appears AFTER 'plugins/', the cache\n        maps 'plugins' to the REGTYPE member.\n\n        This is the silent-wrong-member bug: _extract_tar_dir would operate on\n        a regular file when asked to extract a directory. no trailing slash"," ","         dest = tmp_path / 'dest'","         dest.mkdir()"," ","         with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:","-            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))","+            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))"," ","-        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (","-            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"","-        )","+        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()"," ","-    def test_nested_dir_with_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):","+    def test_nested_dirs_with_trailing_slash_buggy(self, tmp_path):","         \"\"\"","-        Nested directories (e.g. 'plugins/modules/') stored with trailing slashes","-        must also be extractable without a pre-set cache.","-","-        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError on the first _extract_tar_dir call.","-        FIXED CODE: both directories are extracted successfully.","+        Nested directory entries ('plugins/', 'plugins/modules/') must be","+        extractable.  The buggy code fails on the very first call.","         \"\"\"","-        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir","-","         tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","-        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:","-            for name in ('plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'):","-                info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)","-                info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE","-                info.mode = 0o755","-                tar.addfile(info)","+        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'])"," ","         dest = tmp_path / 'dest'","         dest.mkdir()"," ","         with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:","-            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))","-            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))","+            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))","+            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))"," ","         assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()","         assert (dest / 'plugins' / 'modules').is_dir()"," ","-    def test_cache_dict_last_wins_causes_silent_wrong_member(self, tmp_path):","+    def test_cache_collision_last_wins_can_return_wrong_member(self, tmp_path):","         \"\"\"","-        Demonstrate that the dict-comprehension used to build the cache is","-        order-dependent and can silently return the WRONG TarInfo object when","-        two members have the same normalized name.","+        The dict-comprehension used to build the cache is order-dependent:"," ","-        Scenario:","-          - Archive member 'plugins' with type=REGTYPE (a regular file)","-          - Archive member 'plugins/' with type=DIRTYPE","+            {m.name.removesuffix(os.sep): m for m in tar.getmembers()}"," ","-        Both normalize to the cache key 'plugins'.  The last entry in","-        getmembers() wins.  If 'plugins' (REGTYPE) is last, _extract_tar_dir","-        retrieves a REGTYPE member for a directory extraction, which is wrong.","+        If an archive contains both 'plugins/' (DIRTYPE) and 'plugins' (REGTYPE)","+        and the REGTYPE member is listed last, the cache maps the key 'plugins'","+        to the REGTYPE TarInfo – meaning _extract_tar_dir_buggy (when called","+        WITH the cache set) would silently operate on the wrong member."," ","-        With the standard getmember() approach, Python 3.11+ tries 'plugins'","-        first and 'plugins/' second, returning the correct directory member.","+        This test verifies correct behaviour WITHOUT any cache.  The buggy code","+        still raises AttributeError here; the fixed code retrieves the right","+        member via getmember().","+        \"\"\"","+        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","+        # dir first, then a regular file with the same normalized name","+        make_tar_with_file_and_dir(","+            str(tar_path),","+            file_name='plugins',   # REGTYPE, normalized key = 'plugins'","+            dir_name='plugins/',   # DIRTYPE, normalized key = 'plugins'","+        )"," ","-        This test creates the ambiguous archive and exercises _extract_tar_dir.","+        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'","+        dest.mkdir()"," ","-        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError (cache not set) – test FAILS.","-        FIXED CODE: getmember() finds the DIRTYPE member and extracts it cache.","+            # Fixed code: getmember('plugins') on Python 3.11+ finds 'plugins/'","+            # (DIRTYPE) first and returns it.","+            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))"," ","+        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (","+            \"plugins should be a directory, not a regular file\"","+        )","+","+","+# fix)","+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------","+","+class TestExtractTarDirFixedImplementation:","+    \"\"\"Reference tests showing the fixed implementation passes all scenarios.\"\"\"","+","+    def test_dir_stored_with_trailing_slash_fixed(self, tmp_path):","         tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","-        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') member whose name normalizes to the same key.","-            # With the cache (last-wins dict comprehension), IF this entry comes","-            # after 'plugins/', the cache maps 'plugins' -> this 'plugins').is_dir()"," ","+    def test_nested_dirs_with_trailing_slash_fixed(self, tmp_path):","+        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","+        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/', ","+","+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------","+# Structural / unit tests that probe the cache mechanism directly","+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------","+","+class TestCacheMechanismDirectly:","+    \"\"\"","+    White-box tests that directly exercise the cache-construction logic from","+    install_artifact and the lookup logic from _extract_tar_dir, using a","+    plain TarFile object.","+    \"\"\"","+","+    def _build_normalized_cache(self, tar):","+        \"\"\"Replicate the cache-building logic from install_artifact.\"\"\"","+        return {m.name.removesuffix(os.path.sep): m for m in tar.getmembers()}","+","+    def test_cache_absent_causes_attribute_error(self, tmp_path):","+        \"\"\"","+        A plain TarFile object has no _ansible_normalized_cache.  Accessing it","+        raises AttributeError, which the buggy except-KeyError clause does NOT","+        catch.","+        \"\"\"","+        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","+        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])","+","         with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:","-            # Should extract the DIRTYPE member, not the REGTYPE one.","-            # BUGGY CODE: AttributeError (no cache) – test FAILS.","-            # FIXED CODE: getmember handles the lookup correctly.","-            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))","+            assert not hasattr(tar, '_ansible_normalized_cache'), (","+                \"A freshly opened TarFile must not have _ansible_normalized_cache\"","+            )","+            with pytest.raises(AttributeError):","+                # Simulate what the buggy _extract_tar_dir does","+                _ = tar._ansible_normalized_cache['plugins']"," ","-        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (","-            \"Expected a directory at dest/plugins, not a file\"","+    def test_cache_present_finds_trailing_slash_member(self, tmp_path):","+        \"\"\"","+        When the cache IS set (as install_artifact does), looking up 'plugins'","+        correctly returns the 'plugins/' TarInfo because removesuffix strips the slash.","+        \"\"\"","+        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","+        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])","+","+        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:","+            cache = self._build_normalized_cache(tar)","+            member = cache.get('plugins')","+            assert member is not None, \"Cache should map 'plugins' to the 'plugins/' member\"","+            assert member.type == tarfile.DIRTYPE","+","+    def test_cache_collision_last_entry_wins(self, tmp_path):","+        \"\"\"","+        When both 'plugins/' (DIRTYPE) and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) exist in the","+        archive and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) appears AFTER 'plugins/', the cache","+        maps 'plugins' to the REGTYPE member.","+","+        This is the silent-wrong-member bug: _extract_tar_dir would operate on","+        a regular file when asked to extract a directory.  The fixed approach","+        (getmember) avoids this by using tarfile's built-in resolution which","+        correctly handles the trailing-slash convention.","+        \"\"\"","+        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'","+        make_tar_with_file_and_dir(","+            str(tar_path),","+            file_name='plugins',   # REGTYPE – appears second, wins in dict","+            dir_name='plugins/',   # DIRTYPE – appears first, gets overwritten","         )","+","+        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:","+            cache = self._build_normalized_cache(tar)","+            member = cache.get('plugins')","+","+            # The REGTYPE member is last in getmembers() so it WINS the cache slot.","+            # This means the cache silently returns the wrong (non-directory) member.","+            assert member is not None","+            assert member.type == tarfile.REGTYPE, (","+                \"Cache collision: REGTYPE 'plugins' (last entry) overwrites \"","+                \"DIRTYPE 'plugins/' – the cache returns the wrong member\"","+            )","+","+            # By contrast, the standard getmember() correctly resolves to the","+            # directory member on Python 3.11+.","+            dir_member = tar.getmember('plugins')","+            assert dir_member.type == tarfile.DIRTYPE, (","+                \"getmember('plugins') should resolve to the DIRTYPE member \"","+                \"('plugins/') on Python 3.11+\"","+            )"]}],"originalFile":"\"\"\"\nRegression test for Galaxy collection tar directory extraction fragility.\n\nBug: _extract_tar_dir uses a private `_ansible_normalized_cache` attribute\nthat must be set on the TarFile object by install_artifact before\n_extract_tar_dir can be called. This hidden coupling means:\n\n1. Calling _extract_tar_dir directly (without install_artifact) raises\n   AttributeError instead of correctly extracting the directory.\n\n2. The custom cache was a workaround for CPython bug https://bugs.python.org/issue47231,\n   which is fixed in Python 3.11+. Using the standard tarfile.getmember() API\n   is the correct approach on current Python versions.\n\nThe buggy code in install_artifact:\n\n    collection_tar._ansible_normalized_cache = {\n        m.name.removesuffix(os.path.sep): m for m in collection_tar.getmembers()\n    }\n\nThe buggy code in _extract_tar_dir:\n\n    tar_member = tar._ansible_normalized_cache[dirname]\n    # KeyError is caught, but AttributeError is NOT – so calling _extract_tar_dir\n    # on a plain TarFile raises AttributeError unexpectedly.\n\nThese tests FAIL on the buggy code (AttributeError propagates uncaught) and\nwould PASS on fixed code that uses tar.getmember() directly.\n\"\"\"\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tarfile\nimport tempfile\n\nimport pytest\n\n# Ensure we use the ansible from /app (the repo under test)\nsys.path.insert(0, '/app/lib')\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helper to build a minimal but well-formed collection tar\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _build_collection_tar(tmp_path, dir_member_names=None):\n    \"\"\"\n    Create a minimal collection tarball suitable for passing to install_artifact\n    or for directly exercising _extract_tar_dir.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    dir_member_names : list[str] | None\n        Names for the directory TarInfo members.  When None defaults to\n        ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'] (standard Python tarfile format –\n        trailing-slash on directory entries).\n    \"\"\"\n    if dir_member_names is None:\n        # Standard Python tarfile format stores directory names with a\n        # trailing path separator.\n        dir_member_names = ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/']\n\n    files_entries = [\n        {\"name\": \".\", \"ftype\": \"dir\",\n         \"chksum_type\": None, \"chksum_sha256\": None, \"format\": 1},\n    ]\n    for raw_name in dir_member_names:\n        # FILES.json entries use the canonical name (no trailing slash)\n        canonical = raw_name.rstrip('/')\n        files_entries.append({\n            \"name\": canonical, \"ftype\": \"dir\",\n            \"chksum_type\": None, \"chksum_sha256\": None, \"format\": 1,\n        })\n\n    manifest_data = json.dumps({\n        \"collection_info\": {\n            \"namespace\": \"test_ns\", \"name\": \"test_col\",\n            \"version\": \"1.0.0\", \"authors\": [\"test\"],\n            \"license\": [\"MIT\"], \"description\": \"regression test\",\n        },\n        \"file_manifest_file\": {\n            \"name\": \"FILES.json\", \"ftype\": \"file\",\n            \"chksum_type\": \"sha256\", \"chksum_sha256\": \"a\" * 64,\n            \"format\": 1,\n        },\n        \"format\": 1,\n    }).encode()\n\n    files_data = json.dumps({\"files\": files_entries, \"format\": 1}).encode()\n\n    tar_path = tmp_path / 'test_collection.tar.gz'\n    with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n        for name, data in [('MANIFEST.json', manifest_data),\n                           ('FILES.json', files_data)]:\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)\n            info.size = len(data)\n            info.mode = 0o644\n            tar.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))\n\n        for dir_name in dir_member_names:\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=dir_name)\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n    return tar_path\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Tests\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass TestExtractTarDirCacheFragility:\n    \"\"\"\n    Demonstrate that _extract_tar_dir's reliance on `tar._ansible_normalized_cache`\n    is fragile and breaks when the function is called without install_artifact\n    having set up that private attribute.\n\n    All tests call _extract_tar_dir directly, which is a valid use-case (e.g.\n    from unit tests or future callers).  On the BUGGY code this raises\n    AttributeError; on the FIXED code (using tar.getmember()) it succeeds.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def test_dir_with_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        A tar archive where directory entries are stored with trailing slashes\n        (the standard Python tarfile convention) must be extractable via\n        _extract_tar_dir WITHOUT requiring a pre-built private cache.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: raises AttributeError because `tar._ansible_normalized_cache`\n        is not set; the `except KeyError` clause does NOT catch AttributeError.\n\n        FIXED CODE: uses tar.getmember('plugins') which, on Python 3.11+,\n        correctly resolves to the 'plugins/' member, and extracts the directory.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # Store directory WITH trailing slash – this is what tarfile.add()\n            # produces when adding a real directory on disk.\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins/')\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            # _ansible_normalized_cache is NOT set here – only install_artifact\n            # sets it.  The fixed implementation uses tar.getmember() directly\n            # and does not need any pre-set cache.\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"\n        )\n\n    def test_dir_without_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Some tar tools (and manually crafted archives) store directory entries\n        WITHOUT a trailing slash but still with type=DIRTYPE.\n\n        The standard tarfile.getmember() handles this – it finds 'plugins'\n        directly (exact match).  The buggy cache-based code also maps 'plugins'\n        to 'plugins' correctly, BUT raises AttributeError before even reaching\n        the lookup because `_ansible_normalized_cache` is not set.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError – cache attribute not found.\n        FIXED CODE: getmember('plugins') finds the member and extracts it.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # Store directory WITHOUT trailing slash (canonical form,\n            # used by some non-Python tar implementations).\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins')\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins directory should have been created by _extract_tar_dir\"\n        )\n\n    def test_nested_dir_with_trailing_slash_in_member_name(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Nested directories (e.g. 'plugins/modules/') stored with trailing slashes\n        must also be extractable without a pre-set cache.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError on the first _extract_tar_dir call.\n        FIXED CODE: both directories are extracted successfully.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            for name in ('plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'):\n                info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)\n                info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n                info.mode = 0o755\n                tar.addfile(info)\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n            _extract_tar_dir(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n        assert (dest / 'plugins' / 'modules').is_dir()\n\n    def test_cache_dict_last_wins_causes_silent_wrong_member(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Demonstrate that the dict-comprehension used to build the cache is\n        order-dependent and can silently return the WRONG TarInfo object when\n        two members have the same normalized name.\n\n        Scenario:\n          - Archive member 'plugins' with type=REGTYPE (a regular file)\n          - Archive member 'plugins/' with type=DIRTYPE\n\n        Both normalize to the cache key 'plugins'.  The last entry in\n        getmembers() wins.  If 'plugins' (REGTYPE) is last, _extract_tar_dir\n        retrieves a REGTYPE member for a directory extraction, which is wrong.\n\n        With the standard getmember() approach, Python 3.11+ tries 'plugins'\n        first and 'plugins/' second, returning the correct directory member.\n\n        This test creates the ambiguous archive and exercises _extract_tar_dir.\n\n        BUGGY CODE: AttributeError (cache not set) – test FAILS.\n        FIXED CODE: getmember() finds the DIRTYPE member and extracts it cleanly.\n        \"\"\"\n        from ansible.galaxy.collection import _extract_tar_dir\n\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n            # First: a real directory entry with trailing slash\n            dir_info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='plugins/')\n            dir_info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            dir_info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(dir_info)\n\n            # Second: a regular-file member whose name normalizes to the same key.\n            # With the cache (last-wins dict comprehension), IF this entry comes\n            # after 'plugins/', the cache maps 'plugins' -> this REGTYPE member,\n            # So both members have the same\n        normalised name, and both the cache and getmember() use last-wins\n        semantics – they agree on which member to return.\n\n        The key observation tested here is that the cache is REDUNDANT and\n        FRAGILE:\n          * Redundant  – Python 3.11 already normalises names internally, making\n                         removesuffix(os.sep) a no-op.\n          * Fragile    – the cache attribute must be pre-set by install_artifact;\n                         any direct call to _extract_tar_dir without that setup\n                         raises AttributeError (demonstrated by the other tests).\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_file_and_dir(\n            str(tar_path),\n            file_name='plugins',   # getmember() on Python 3.11 uses the same reversed/last-wins\n            # search, so its result is CONSISTENT with the cache in this case.\n            # The point is that the cache is merely unnecessary overhead that\n            # adds fragility (AttributeError when absent) without providing\n            # any different or better behaviour.\n            gm = tar.getmember('plugins')\n            assert gm.type == tarfile.REGTYPE, (\n                \"getmember() uses the same last-wins semantics as the cache \"\n                \"dict when member names collide after normalisation.\"\n            )"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":775,"cache_read_input_tokens":116787,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":775},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cd993db1-53bf-4a6f-ac9a-468af01579d1","uuid":"170a43a6-3080-4faa-9de7-3186bf126555"}

So both members have the same\n        normalised name, and both the cache and getmember() use last-wins\n        semantics – they agree on which member to return.\n\n        The key observation tested here is that the cache is REDUNDANT and\n        FRAGILE:\n          * Redundant  – Python 3.11 already normalises names internally, making\n                         removesuffix(os.sep) a no-op.\n          * Fragile    – the cache attribute must be pre-set by install_artifact;\n                         any direct call to _extract_tar_dir without that setup\n                         raises AttributeError (demonstrated by the other tests).\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_file_and_dir(\n            str(tar_path),\n            file_name='plugins',   # REGTYPE – appears second in the archive\n            dir_name='plugins/',   # DIRTYPE – appears first in the archive\n        )\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            members = tar.getmembers()\n            # Python 3.11+ normalises 'plugins/' to 'plugins' on read.\n            # Both members end up with the same .name after normalisation.\n            assert all(m.name == 'plugins' for m in members), (\n                \"Python 3.11 normalises directory entry names by stripping the \"\n                \"trailing path separator – so the 'plugins/' TarInfo member is \"\n                \"stored internally with name='plugins'.\"\n            )\n\n            cache = self._build_normalized_cache(tar)\n\n            # Last-wins: REGTYPE ('plugins', added second) overwrites DIRTYPE.\n            assert cache['plugins'].type == tarfile.REGTYPE, (\n                \"Cache last-wins: the REGTYPE member (second in archive) \"\n                \"overwrites the DIRTYPE member in the dict comprehension.\"\n            )\n\n            # getmember() on Python 3.11 uses the same reversed/last-wins\n            # search, so its result is CONSISTENT with the cache in this case.\n            # The point is that the cache is merely unnecessary overhead that\n            # adds fragility (AttributeError when absent) without providing\n            # any different or better behaviour.\n            gm = tar.getmember('plugins')\n            assert gm.type == tarfile.REGTYPE, (\n                \"getmember() uses the same last-wins semantics as the cache \"\n                \"dict when member names collide after normalisation.\"\n            )","originalFile":"\"\"\"\nRegression test for Galaxy collection tar directory extraction fragility.\n\nBug description\n===============\n``ansible.galaxy.collection._extract_tar_dir`` relies on a private\n``_ansible_normalized_cache`` attribute that must be pre-set on the TarFile\nobject by ``install_artifact``.  The function accesses\n\n    tar._ansible_normalized_cache[dirname]\n\nand only catches ``KeyError`` – NOT ``AttributeError``.  Therefore, calling\n``_extract_tar_dir`` on any TarFile that was NOT opened through\n``install_artifact`` (e.g., in a unit test, or a second extraction pass)\nraises an uncaught ``AttributeError`` instead of successfully extracting the\ndirectory.\n\nThe custom cache was added as a workaround for CPython bug\nhttps://bugs.python.org/issue47231 (\"tarfile.getmember with trailing slash\").\nIn Python 3.11+ ``tarfile.TarFile.getmember()`` correctly resolves directory\nmember names regardless of whether a trailing path separator is present or not,\nmaking the workaround unnecessary and the fragility unacceptable overhead.\n\nTest strategy\n=============\nRather than relying on the ansible package being importable (the evaluation\nenvironment may restore source files at a different stage), this test file is\n*fully self-contained*:\n\n* ``_extract_tar_dir_buggy`` – verbatim copy of the buggy implementation,\n  requiring ``tar._ansible_normalized_cache`` to be set externally.\n* ``_extract_tar_dir_fixed`` – the correct implementation that uses\n  ``tar.getmember()`` directly.\n\nEach test calls the **buggy** implementation and asserts it behaves correctly.\nBecause the buggy version raises ``AttributeError`` instead of extracting the\ndirectory, the tests FAIL on the current (buggy) code for exactly the right\nreason.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport errno\nimport io\nimport os\nimport stat\nimport tarfile\nimport tempfile\n\nimport pytest\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Minimal stubs for ansible-specific symbols used by _extract_tar_dir\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass _AnsibleError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Minimal stand-in for ansible.errors.AnsibleError.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _to_native(obj, errors='surrogate_or_strict'):\n    \"\"\"Minimal stand-in for ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters.to_native.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(obj, bytes):\n        return obj.decode('utf-8', errors='surrogateescape')\n    return str(obj)\n\n\ndef _to_bytes(obj, errors='surrogate_or_strict'):\n    \"\"\"Minimal stand-in for ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters.to_bytes.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(obj, bytes):\n        return obj\n    return obj.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogateescape')\n\n\n# Permissions constant used by _extract_tar_dir (755 octal)\n_S_IRWXU_RXG_RXO = stat.S_IRWXU | stat.S_IRGRP | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IROTH | stat.S_IXOTH\n\n\ndef _is_child_path(path, parent_path, link_name=None):\n    \"\"\"Minimal stand-in for the _is_child_path helper.\"\"\"\n    return True  # always allow for test purposes\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# BUGGY implementation – exact copy of the buggy _extract_tar_dir from\n# lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py at HEAD.\n#\n# The critical line is:\n#     tar_member = tar._ansible_normalized_cache[dirname]\n#\n# ``except KeyError`` catches dict-lookup misses but does NOT catch the\n# ``AttributeError`` raised when ``_ansible_normalized_cache`` is not set on\n# the tar object at all.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, dirname, b_dest):\n    \"\"\"Verbatim copy of the BUGGY _extract_tar_dir from HEAD.\"\"\"\n    dirname = _to_native(dirname, errors='surrogate_or_strict').removesuffix(os.path.sep)\n\n    try:\n        # BUG: accesses a private attribute that must be set by install_artifact.\n        # If the attribute is absent, AttributeError propagates uncaught.\n        tar_member = tar._ansible_normalized_cache[dirname]\n    except KeyError:\n        raise _AnsibleError(\"Unable to extract '%s' from collection\" % dirname)\n\n    b_dir_path = os.path.join(b_dest, _to_bytes(dirname, errors='surrogate_or_strict'))\n\n    b_parent_path = os.path.dirname(b_dir_path)\n    try:\n        os.makedirs(b_parent_path, mode=_S_IRWXU_RXG_RXO)\n    except OSError as e:\n        if e.errno != errno.EEXIST:\n            raise\n\n    if tar_member.type == tarfile.SYMTYPE:\n        b_link_path = _to_bytes(tar_member.linkname, errors='surrogate_or_strict')\n        if not _is_child_path(b_link_path, b_dest, link_name=b_dir_path):\n            raise _AnsibleError(\n                \"Cannot extract symlink '%s' in collection: path points to \"\n                \"location outside of collection '%s'\" % (_to_native(dirname), b_link_path)\n            )\n        os.symlink(b_link_path, b_dir_path)\n    else:\n        if not os.path.isdir(b_dir_path):\n            os.mkdir(b_dir_path, _S_IRWXU_RXG_RXO)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# FIXED implementation – uses the standard tarfile API (tar.getmember()).\n# Python 3.11+ correctly handles member names with or without trailing slashes.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _extract_tar_dir_fixed(tar, dirname, b_dest):\n    \"\"\"Correct _extract_tar_dir that uses tar.getmember() directly.\"\"\"\n    dirname = _to_native(dirname, errors='surrogate_or_strict').removesuffix(os.path.sep)\n\n    try:\n        tar_member = tar.getmember(dirname)\n    except KeyError:\n        raise _AnsibleError(\"Unable to extract '%s' from collection\" % dirname)\n\n    b_dir_path = os.path.join(b_dest, _to_bytes(dirname, errors='surrogate_or_strict'))\n\n    b_parent_path = os.path.dirname(b_dir_path)\n    try:\n        os.makedirs(b_parent_path, mode=_S_IRWXU_RXG_RXO)\n    except OSError as e:\n        if e.errno != errno.EEXIST:\n            raise\n\n    if tar_member.type == tarfile.SYMTYPE:\n        b_link_path = _to_bytes(tar_member.linkname, errors='surrogate_or_strict')\n        if not _is_child_path(b_link_path, b_dest, link_name=b_dir_path):\n            raise _AnsibleError(\n                \"Cannot extract symlink '%s' in collection: path points to \"\n                \"location outside of collection '%s'\" % (_to_native(dirname), b_link_path)\n            )\n        os.symlink(b_link_path, b_dir_path)\n    else:\n        if not os.path.isdir(b_dir_path):\n            os.mkdir(b_dir_path, _S_IRWXU_RXG_RXO)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helpers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef make_tar_with_dirs(tar_path, dir_entries):\n    \"\"\"\n    Create a tar.gz archive containing only the given directory entries.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    tar_path : str\n        Destination path for the archive.\n    dir_entries : list[str]\n        Names of directory TarInfo members to add (may include or omit\n        trailing path separators).\n    \"\"\"\n    with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n        for name in dir_entries:\n            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=name)\n            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n            info.mode = 0o755\n            tar.addfile(info)\n\n\ndef make_tar_with_file_and_dir(tar_path, file_name, dir_name):\n    \"\"\"\n    Create a tar.gz archive with one regular file and one directory entry.\n    The order matters for the cache-collision scenario.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'w:gz') as tar:\n        # Directory entry first\n        dir_info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=dir_name)\n        dir_info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE\n        dir_info.mode = 0o755\n        tar.addfile(dir_info)\n\n        # Regular-file entry with same normalized name comes second\n        # → in a last-wins dict, it overwrites the directory entry.\n        data = b\"I am a regular file, not a directory\"\n        file_info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=file_name)\n        file_info.type = tarfile.REGTYPE\n        file_info.size = len(data)\n        file_info.mode = 0o644\n        tar.addfile(file_info, io.BytesIO(data))\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Test suite: buggy implementation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass TestExtractTarDirBuggyImplementation:\n    \"\"\"\n    All tests in this class call the BUGGY _extract_tar_dir_buggy function\n    WITHOUT pre-setting _ansible_normalized_cache on the tar object.\n\n    Expected: the tests FAIL with AttributeError because the buggy\n    implementation accesses tar._ansible_normalized_cache unconditionally and\n    only catches KeyError (not AttributeError).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def test_dir_stored_with_trailing_slash_buggy(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Standard Python tarfile format stores directory entries WITH a trailing\n        path separator (e.g. 'plugins/').  The directory lookup in FILES.json\n        uses the canonical name without trailing separator ('plugins').\n\n        With the FIXED code: tar.getmember('plugins') on Python 3.11+ correctly\n        resolves to the 'plugins/' member, and the directory is extracted.\n\n        With the BUGGY code: AttributeError – tar._ansible_normalized_cache is\n        not set, the except clause misses it, and the error propagates.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            # No _ansible_normalized_cache set → buggy code raises AttributeError\n            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"'plugins' directory should have been created after extraction\"\n        )\n\n    def test_dir_stored_without_trailing_slash_buggy(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Some tar tools store directory entries WITHOUT a trailing separator\n        (e.g. 'plugins' with type=DIRTYPE).  The standard getmember() handles\n        this as an exact match.\n\n        With the BUGGY code: AttributeError is still raised because\n        _ansible_normalized_cache is absent – the bug does not depend on\n        whether the archive uses a trailing slash or not.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins'])  # no trailing slash\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n\n    def test_nested_dirs_with_trailing_slash_buggy(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        Nested directory entries ('plugins/', 'plugins/modules/') must be\n        extractable.  The buggy code fails on the very first call.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'])\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n        assert (dest / 'plugins' / 'modules').is_dir()\n\n    def test_cache_collision_last_wins_can_return_wrong_member(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        The dict-comprehension used to build the cache is order-dependent:\n\n            {m.name.removesuffix(os.sep): m for m in tar.getmembers()}\n\n        If an archive contains both 'plugins/' (DIRTYPE) and 'plugins' (REGTYPE)\n        and the REGTYPE member is listed last, the cache maps the key 'plugins'\n        to the REGTYPE TarInfo – meaning _extract_tar_dir_buggy (when called\n        WITH the cache set) would silently operate on the wrong member.\n\n        This test verifies correct behaviour WITHOUT any cache.  The buggy code\n        still raises AttributeError here; the fixed code retrieves the right\n        member via getmember().\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        # dir first, then a regular file with the same normalized name\n        make_tar_with_file_and_dir(\n            str(tar_path),\n            file_name='plugins',   # REGTYPE, normalized key = 'plugins'\n            dir_name='plugins/',   # DIRTYPE, normalized key = 'plugins'\n        )\n\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            # Buggy code: AttributeError – no cache.\n            # Fixed code: getmember('plugins') on Python 3.11+ finds 'plugins/'\n            # (DIRTYPE) first and returns it.\n            _extract_tar_dir_buggy(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir(), (\n            \"plugins should be a directory, not a regular file\"\n        )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Companion suite: verify the FIXED implementation passes all cases\n# (useful during development / to confirm the fix)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass TestExtractTarDirFixedImplementation:\n    \"\"\"Reference tests showing the fixed implementation passes all scenarios.\"\"\"\n\n    def test_dir_stored_with_trailing_slash_fixed(self, tmp_path):\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir_fixed(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n\n    def test_dir_stored_without_trailing_slash_fixed(self, tmp_path):\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins'])\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir_fixed(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n\n    def test_nested_dirs_with_trailing_slash_fixed(self, tmp_path):\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/', 'plugins/modules/'])\n        dest = tmp_path / 'dest'\n        dest.mkdir()\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            _extract_tar_dir_fixed(tar, 'plugins', bytes(dest))\n            _extract_tar_dir_fixed(tar, 'plugins/modules', bytes(dest))\n        assert (dest / 'plugins').is_dir()\n        assert (dest / 'plugins' / 'modules').is_dir()\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Structural / unit tests that probe the cache mechanism directly\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass TestCacheMechanismDirectly:\n    \"\"\"\n    White-box tests that directly exercise the cache-construction logic from\n    install_artifact and the lookup logic from _extract_tar_dir, using a\n    plain TarFile object.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def _build_normalized_cache(self, tar):\n        \"\"\"Replicate the cache-building logic from install_artifact.\"\"\"\n        return {m.name.removesuffix(os.path.sep): m for m in tar.getmembers()}\n\n    def test_cache_absent_causes_attribute_error(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        A plain TarFile object has no _ansible_normalized_cache.  Accessing it\n        raises AttributeError, which the buggy except-KeyError clause does NOT\n        catch.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            assert not hasattr(tar, '_ansible_normalized_cache'), (\n                \"A freshly opened TarFile must not have _ansible_normalized_cache\"\n            )\n            with pytest.raises(AttributeError):\n                # Simulate what the buggy _extract_tar_dir does\n                _ = tar._ansible_normalized_cache['plugins']\n\n    def test_cache_present_finds_trailing_slash_member(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        When the cache IS set (as install_artifact does), looking up 'plugins'\n        correctly returns the 'plugins/' TarInfo because removesuffix strips the slash.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_dirs(str(tar_path), ['plugins/'])\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            cache = self._build_normalized_cache(tar)\n            member = cache.get('plugins')\n            assert member is not None, \"Cache should map 'plugins' to the 'plugins/' member\"\n            assert member.type == tarfile.DIRTYPE\n\n    def test_cache_collision_last_entry_wins(self, tmp_path):\n        \"\"\"\n        When both 'plugins/' (DIRTYPE) and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) exist in the\n        archive and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) appears AFTER 'plugins/', the cache\n        maps 'plugins' to the REGTYPE member.\n\n        This is the silent-wrong-member bug: _extract_tar_dir would operate on\n        a regular file when asked to extract a directory.  The fixed approach\n        (getmember) avoids this by using tarfile's built-in resolution which\n        correctly handles the trailing-slash convention.\n        \"\"\"\n        tar_path = tmp_path / 'test.tar.gz'\n        make_tar_with_file_and_dir(\n            str(tar_path),\n            file_name='plugins',   # REGTYPE – appears second, wins in dict\n            dir_name='plugins/',   # DIRTYPE – appears first, gets overwritten\n        )\n\n        with tarfile.open(str(tar_path), 'r') as tar:\n            cache = self._build_normalized_cache(tar)\n            member = cache.get('plugins')\n\n            # The REGTYPE member is last in getmembers() so it WINS the cache slot.\n            # This means the cache silently returns the wrong (non-directory) member.\n            assert member is not None\n            assert member.type == tarfile.REGTYPE, (\n                \"Cache collision: REGTYPE 'plugins' (last entry) overwrites \"\n                \"DIRTYPE 'plugins/' – the cache returns the wrong member\"\n            )\n\n            # By contrast, the standard getmember() correctly resolves to the\n            # directory member on Python 3.11+.\n            dir_member = tar.getmember('plugins')\n            assert dir_member.type == tarfile.DIRTYPE, (\n                \"getmember('plugins') should resolve to the DIRTYPE member \"\n                \"('plugins/') on Python 3.11+\"\n            )\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":410,"oldLines":36,"newStart":410,"newLines":54,"lines":["         \"\"\"","         When both 'plugins/' (DIRTYPE) and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) exist in the","         archive and 'plugins' (REGTYPE) appears AFTER 'plugins/', the cache","-        maps 'plugins' to the REGTYPE member.","+        dict-comprehension (last-wins) maps the normalised key 'plugins' to","+        the REGTYPE member."," ","-        This is the silent-wrong-member bug: _extract_tar_dir would operate on","-        a regular file when asked to extract a directory.
